Attention, sentiment, entities, documents

One attention head computed by hand, then three jobs a bank gives a language model: reading sentiment, finding names and amounts, and pulling fields out of documents.

InstructorDr. Arun B Ayyar
WithDr. Nirav Bhatt
Duration90 minutes
Data11,931 finance headlines · simulated sentences, pages, loan agreements
Codeadvanced_nlp_for_finance.ipynb
Plan

Plan for the 90 minutes Four blocks. Every number on the slides comes from the notebook, which runs in a few minutes on a free Colab GPU.

minutes from the start
One model family. Every model today is a transformer encoder of the BERT family, between 33 and 125 million weights. The first block opens one up; the other three put it to work.
One question per block. How far does a model get as it comes, and what do labelled examples from the bank’s own text add?
The headlines are a public dataset. The sentences, pages and loan agreements are simulated by make_data.py; no text comes from a real bank or a real company.
Tokens · Example

Example The model reads word pieces. Its vocabulary holds 30,522 pieces, and a word that is missing from it is spelled out of smaller ones.

DistilBERT tokenizer, uncased
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    'distilbert-base-uncased')
tok.tokenize('remortgage')
No word is unknown. A term the model has never seen still reaches it, in pieces. Whether the pieces mean anything together is learned from the bank’s text.
Limits count pieces. A 512-token limit is a limit on pieces. "remortgage" spends 5 of them.
Case is gone. This tokenizer lowercases, so EBITDA and SONIA lose their capitals. A cased model keeps them, which matters for names.
Model · Concept

Concept A transformer encoder turns a sentence into one vector per token. DistilBERT does it with 66 million weights in 6 layers.

DistilBERT, left to right

Vectors

Each piece is looked up in a table of 768 numbers. A second table adds the position, 1 to 512.

Attention

Every token takes a weighted average of all the tokens. The weights are computed from the tokens themselves.

Feed-forward

A small network reshapes each token’s vector on its own. Attention and feed-forward make one layer.

Task head

One linear layer on top: a class for the sentence, a tag for each token, or the start and end of an answer.

Attention · Intuition

Intuition To represent "its", the model has to find what "its" refers to. In layer 3, head 11, "its" puts 78.2% of its weight on "bank".

"The bank raised its base rate after inflation rose." · attention from "its", layer 3, head 11
The twelve weights add to 1. Line width is the weight.
No labels for this. The model was trained only to fill in hidden words. A head that links a pronoun to its noun appeared because it helps with that task.
A weight is a share. The new vector for "its" is a weighted average of all twelve token vectors, and here 78.2% of it is the vector of "bank".
Attention · Mechanism

Mechanism One head, one token, three steps. The row is "its"; every number is read out of the model.

layer 3, head 11

1. Score

Each token’s vector is multiplied by two learned matrices to give a query q and a key k of 64 numbers. The score is the dot product of the query of "its" with each key, divided by √64 = 8.

2. Softmax

Exponentiate the scores and divide by their sum. A gap of 1.92 in score between "bank" and the runner-up becomes a weight of 0.782 against 0.115.

3. Weighted sum

A third matrix gives each token a value v. The output for "its" is the sum of the values, each multiplied by its weight.

Attention · Mechanism

Mechanism continued 1 The three steps for all tokens at once are one line of matrix algebra. The notebook computes it by hand and gets the model’s own numbers.

Attention(Q, K, V)  =  softmax( Q KT / √d ) · V
symbolwhat it isshape here
Qqueries: one row per token12 × 64
Kkeys: one row per token12 × 64
Vvalues: one row per token12 × 64
dnumbers in a query or key64
Q KTevery token scored against every token12 × 12
softmaxeach row turned into weights that add to 112 × 12
att = enc.transformer.layer[2].attention
h = hidden_states[2][0]        # 12 x 768
Q = att.q_lin(h).view(-1, 12, 64)[:, 10]
K = att.k_lin(h).view(-1, 12, 64)[:, 10]
scores  = (Q @ K.T) / 64 ** 0.5
weights = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
assert torch.allclose(weights, model_attention)
The assert passes: the hand computation and the model agree to four decimal places.
Why divide by √d. Dot products of longer vectors are larger, and large scores push the softmax to put all the weight on one token. Dividing keeps the scores in a range where the weights can still be trained.
Attention · Mechanism

Mechanism continued 2 A layer runs 12 heads side by side, each with its own Q, K and V, and the model stacks 6 layers: 72 heads, each attending to something different.

browser JS
click a token to see where it looks
On these sentences, 4 heads in layers 1 and 2 put over half their weight on the next or previous token. In layers 3 to 5, 26 of the 36 heads put over half on [SEP], where a head parks its weight when it has nothing to do.
Attention · Example

Example The word "bank" in six sentences. Going in, the six vectors are nearly the same (0.96 across senses). After six layers of attention, the two senses have separated (0.59).

cosine similarity between the vectors for "bank"
Blue rows are the money sense, green rows the river sense.
1The bank raised its base rate after inflation rose.
2She moved her savings to another bank last month.
3The bank approved the loan within two days.
4They walked along the bank of the river at dusk.
5The boat was tied to the muddy bank.
6Reeds grew thick on the far bank of the stream.
same sense, after 6 layers0.86
different sense, after 6 layers0.59
This is what a classifier reads. Sentiment, entity tags and extracted spans are all computed from these context-dependent vectors.
Attention · Drawbacks

Drawbacks Every token attends to every token, so a head holds n² weights for n tokens. At 512 tokens that is 262,144 weights a head, 18.9 million across the 72 heads.

one batch of 16 texts through DistilBERT, GPU
16 times the tokens took 13 times as long here; the attention cells grew 256 times.
A hard limit of 512 pieces. The position table has 512 rows. A longer document is cut, or split into chunks that are scored one at a time.
A cut loses the end. The governing-law clause of a contract sits on the last page. Truncation to the first 512 pieces never shows it to the model.
A weight is not an explanation. A head that looks at "bank" shows where information came from. It does not show how the model used it.
Model · Concept

Concept continued 1 The same attention, with one change, gives the two families in use today. An encoder reads; a decoder writes.

which weights are allowed
encoder (BERT family)decoder (GPT family)
trained tofill in hidden wordspredict the next word
outputa vector per tokentext, one token at a time
size today0.03 to 0.4 billion weights0.5 to hundreds of billions
used forclassify, tag, extract, embedanswer, summarise, write
sessionthis onethe next one
Why encoders still matter. A fixed label set, millions of rows a day and a latency budget in milliseconds describe most text jobs in a bank. An encoder of 66 million weights does them on a CPU.

Sentiment · Concept

Concept A pretrained encoder can be used three ways. They differ in which weights the bank’s own labels are allowed to change.

which weights are trained

As it comes

Download a model that already has a sentiment head. Nothing is trained. Its labels and its idea of "negative" come from its own training data.

Frozen embeddings

Run each text through the model once and keep the vector. Train a small linear model on the vectors. Seconds on a CPU once the vectors exist.

Fine-tuning

Put a new head on the model and train all the weights on the labelled rows for a few passes. Needs a GPU and the most labels.

Sentiment · Example

Example Two models used as they come, against a bag-of-words baseline trained on the 9,543 labelled rows. The baseline scores 0.773; the better of the two downloads scores 0.660.

macro-F1 on the test rows
General tweet model. RoBERTa trained on 124 million general tweets. Its "negative" is an unhappy author, which a profit warning written in neutral words is not.
FinBERT. BERT trained on financial news sentences. Right domain, different text: full sentences from news wires, where these rows are clipped headlines with tickers.
TF-IDF and logistic regression has no idea what a word means, and has read 9,543 rows of exactly this text. Here that is worth +0.113 macro-F1 over the better download.

Analyst actions. "Cuts to Hold" holds no emotional word. To an investor it is a downgrade.
Plain verbs. "Pulls outlook" and "cools on" read as neutral statements. The label comes from what the event does to the share price, which a model trained on general tweets never saw.

Sentiment · Example

Example continued 2 The two methods that train on the labelled rows. Fine-tuning DistilBERT reaches 0.844 macro-F1 in 95 seconds on a GPU.

macro-F1 on the test rows
Embeddings and a linear model: 0.738. One pass of a 33-million-weight embedding model over all rows took 7 seconds. The vectors can be reused for search and clustering.
Fine-tuning: 0.844. Three passes over the training rows, every weight updated. +0.071 over the bag-of-words baseline and +0.184 over the better download.
Frozen vectors lose to word counts here (0.738 against 0.773). A general-purpose embedding has no dimension for "downgrade".
Sentiment · Test

Test The fine-tuned model on the 2,388 test rows. The largest error cell is 87 bullish rows read as neutral.

rows: label, columns: prediction
F1, bearish0.793
F1, bullish0.822
F1, neutral0.916
Read the rows. Of 347 bearish rows the model finds 286. Of 475 bullish rows it finds 374. Neutral, the class with the most training rows, takes 51 of the 61 bearish misses and 87 of the 101 bullish misses.
Which error costs more depends on the use. A news-alert feed can live with a missed bearish headline. A model that feeds a trading signal treats bearish read as bullish as the expensive cell.

Drawbacks The fine-tuned model is still wrong on 12.0% of test rows. Six of them, with the label and what the model said.

headlinelabelfine-tuned said
Analysts Eviscerate Musk's Cybertruck: "0% Of Responses Felt It Will Be A Success"bearishneutral

One label per headline. "Downgraded at one broker, top pick at another" names two views of one stock. A single label cannot hold both.
Labels are judgements. Whether a routine price-target change is neutral or bullish is a choice the annotators made. A model trained on their labels inherits it.
Vocabulary moves. The training rows come from one period. New tickers, new products and new slang arrive after it, and the score on last year’s test set does not show that.
Entities · Concept

Concept Named entity recognition gives every token a tag. B- opens an entity, I- continues it, O is everything else.

one test sentence, token by token
PERperson   ORGcompany   LOCplace   MONEYamount   DATEdate   ACCTaccount number

Why a bank wants it

Screen payment text against sanctions lists. Find the parties in a contract. Remove personal data from a complaint before it is used for training.

Why tags, not a list

The tagger works on any sentence length and returns where each entity is, so the entity can be highlighted, redacted or linked to a customer record.

Two kinds of entity

Amounts, dates and account numbers have a shape. Names of people, companies and places have no shape and depend on context.

Entities · Data

The tagged sentences, by text type 2,400 training and 800 test sentences, simulated, with 2,531 tagged entities in the test set.

Payment narrative 204 test sentences

FPS CREDIT FROM MATEO CHAUDHRYPER 27 JAN 2024DATE

Case note 201 test sentences

Hollins Dental plcORG , based in PerthLOC , expects turnover of USD 8,701MONEY this year according to Declan KowalskiPER .

News line 207 test sentences

LeedsLOC firm Glenmoor Capital & SonsORG named M KowalskiPER as chair on 9 September 2022DATE .

Complaint 188 test sentences

Nobody in BristolLOC could tell me why £11,207MONEY was sent to Dr Astrid PetrovPER .
The test set is new text. Its sentence patterns, people, companies and places do not appear in the training set. A tagger that memorised the training names scores nothing on them.
Payment narratives are in capitals and have no grammar. They are the text a bank holds most of.
Entities · Test

Test An entity counts as found only when the first token, the last token and the type all match the label. Most of a company name earns nothing.

entity-level scoring
the three scores
precision = found / predicted how much of the output is right recall = found / labelled how much of the truth was found F1 = 2 x precision x recall / (precision + recall)
B drops "Ltd". Its span is counted once as a false entity and once as a missed one. A sanctions screen that matches on the full legal name fails on it.
Token accuracy hides this. Prediction B has 10 of 11 tokens right, and most tokens in any text are O.
Entities · Example

Example Three regular expressions for the entities that have a shape. Over the three types they score F1 0.874 with no training data.

RULES = {
 'MONEY': r'(?:£|(?:GBP|EUR)\s)\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?(?:\s?(?:m|million))?\b'
          r'|\b\d[\d,]*\.\d\d\sGBP\b|\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?\smillion\spounds\b',
 'DATE':  rf'\b\d{1,2}\s{MON}\s\d{4}\b|\b\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}\b'
          rf'|\b\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b|\b{MON}\s\d{1,2},\s\d{4}\b',
 'ACCT':  r'\bGB\d{2}\s[A-Z]{4}(?:\s\d{4}){3}\s\d{2}\b'
          r'|\b\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2}\s\d{8}\b',
}

Cheap, fast and explainable. A rule runs in microseconds and a failed match can be read off the pattern.
A rule knows only the formats it was written for. Each miss here is a format the author did not list, and each new format is another edit.

Capitals carry the signal in news. A model that learned "capitalised word in mid-sentence is a name" has nothing to go on when every word is in capitals.
Its label set is fixed. It has no tag for an amount or an account number, and cannot be asked for one.
Entities · Mechanism

Mechanism Labels are per word and the model reads word pieces. This sentence has 15 words and 21 pieces.

labels on words, then on pieces

The labels

An annotator tags whole words. A company name of three words gets B-ORG, I-ORG, I-ORG.

1. Split

The tokenizer breaks rare words, names above all, into pieces. The tagger outputs one tag per piece.

2. Label the first piece

Each word’s label goes on its first piece. The other 6 pieces are left out of the loss, and at prediction time only first pieces are read.

Company or person. In the first row a person’s name in capitals is tagged as a company. Context settles it in a sentence and is absent in a narrative.

Entities · Verdict

Verdict F1 by entity type for the three approaches. Each approach is absent where it has nothing to offer.

F1 on the test set
 rules    general model, as it comes    fine-tuned tagger
Shaped entities: start with rules. They need no labels and their failures can be read. Keep them as a check on the model even after a tagger exists.
Names: label the bank’s own text. The tagger trained on 2,400 sentences of this kind of text beats the general model on each of the three types they share.
Documents · Concept

Concept A document pipeline is a chain of small decisions. Each press adds a stage, and each stage can be measured on its own.

from a scanned page to a record

Classify

Loan agreement, guarantee, statement or complaint? The type decides which fields to look for and which team owns the page.

Extract

Pull the borrower, the amount, the rate and the dates out of the text, each with a score.

Validate

Checks that need no model: the date parses, the amount is positive, the borrower is a customer on file.

Accept or review

Confident, valid values go straight through. The rest go to a person, and their corrections become training data.

Classification · Data

Pages of eight document types 1,400 training pages and 600 test pages, simulated. A page is a few paragraphs, and the three legal types share boilerplate.

loan agreement

The Lender agrees to make available to the Borrower a term loan facility in an aggregate principal amount of GBP 15,800. Signed for and on behalf of the parties on 1 November 2025. If any provision is found to be une…

If any provision is found to be unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in full force. The Guarantor waives any right to require the Lender to proceed first against the principal debtor. The Guarantor irrevocably guarantees to the Lender the due payment of all sums owed by Halcyon Media Partners.

11 Jan DIRECT DEBIT RAVENSWORTH DENTAL LLP 95.48 balance 659.52 Your deposits are protected up to the limit set by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.

the eight types
account statement annual report card statement complaint letter guarantee kyc form loan agreement mortgage offer
Pages, not documents. Scans arrive as loose pages. A page from the middle of a loan agreement may hold only a notices clause and a governing-law clause, which a guarantee has too.
Classification · Example

Example Three classifiers trained on clean text, tested on pages with scan damage. On clean pages all three score between 0.953 and 0.962; at 20% damage they range from 0.737 to 0.962.

accuracy on the 600 test pages
a page with 10% of characters damaged

Character n-gram tf-idf holds up best. A damaged word still shares most of its character runs with the clean word, so the features survive.
Test on what production sends. A score on clean digital text says little about pages that have been through a scanner and OCR.

Some pages cannot be classified alone. A page of boilerplate belongs to whatever document it came from. The fix is in the pipeline: classify the page together with its neighbours.
Look at the wrong pages before changing the model. Five rows of errors showed a data problem that no larger model would fix.

Fields to extract from a loan agreement 400 simulated loan agreements, about 167 words each. Six values are wanted from each; the underlined values look right and are wrong.

Distractors. An arrangement fee is an amount, a default rate is a rate, a first repayment date is a date, a guarantor, where there is one, is a company. "The first amount in the text" is not a rule that works.
Clauses come in a random order and each has three phrasings, one of them much the commonest.
Extraction · Example

Example One regular expression per field, written against the usual wording. They are right on 56.6% of fields: 100% on the usual wording and 0% on the other two.

RX = {
 'borrower': r'made between (.+?) \(the "Borrower"\)',
 'lender': r'\(the "Borrower"\) and (.+?) \(the "Lender"\)',
 'principal': r'principal amount of (GBP [\d,]+)',
 'rate': r'accrues on the loan at (.+?) per annum',
 'maturity': r'repaid in full on ({DATE})',
 'law': r'governed by the law of (.+?)\.',
}
A rule never returns a wrong value here. It returns the right one or nothing, so every failure is visible and can be sent to a person.
share of agreements with the field right
Coverage is the limit. Each new phrasing needs a new pattern, and the list of phrasings in real contracts has no end.
Extraction · Example

Example continued 1 A question-answering model reads the agreement and one question per field, and returns a span of the text. It has seen no loan agreement, and is right on 85.5% of fields.

one question per field
borrower Who is the borrower? lender Who is the lender? principal What is the principal amount of the loan? rate What is the rate of interest on the loan? maturity On what date must the loan be repaid in full? law Which law governs the agreement?
qa = pipeline('question-answering',
              model='deepset/roberta-base-squad2')
qa(question='Who is the borrower?', context=text)

A wrong answer looks like a right one. It is a real date or a real amount from the page. Only the score, or a second check, separates them.
Extraction · Example

Accept or review, by score Every answer carries a score. Above the threshold the value is accepted unchecked; below it, a person looks. 2,400 answers, green right and red wrong.

answers by score
browser JS
The threshold is a staffing decision. It trades wrong values in the system against pages on a reviewer’s desk. The model gives the curve; operations picks the point.
Check the score before trusting it. A threshold works only if wrong answers have lower scores. Plot this histogram on the bank’s own documents first.
Extraction · Layout, then extractor · Concept

Concept The loan agreements so far arrive as one clean paragraph. A real page has columns, key-value boxes and a table, and its meaning is partly in the positions.

the page, drawn as blocks
text read left to right, line by line
FACILITY AGREEMENT Lender Borrower Halcyon Commercial Valebrook Finance Ltd Freight Interest accrues on The Borrower shall the loan at the rate supply its audited set out below ... accounts within ... Principal Rate Final repayment GBP 1,996,000 8.31% 26 September 2026
The two columns are woven together. “Halcyon Commercial Valebrook” is now one line, and the table is a row of values with no labels beside them.
after a layout model: blocks, types, reading order
1 title FACILITY AGREEMENT 2 key-value Lender: Halcyon Commercial Finance Ltd 3 key-value Borrower: Valebrook Freight 4 text Interest accrues on the loan at the rate set out below ... 5 text The Borrower shall supply its audited accounts within ... 6 table | Principal | GBP 1,996,000 | | Rate | 8.31% | | Final repayment | 26 September 2026 |
Each block has a type and a place in the reading order. The table keeps its cells. This text is what the extractor reads.
The page and both outputs are an illustration, drawn with the values of the first agreement. The notebook does not run a layout model.
Extraction · Layout, then extractor · Mechanism

Mechanism Two models in a row. The first turns the page into ordered, typed text. The second reads that text and returns the fields.

from a page to checked fields
stagewhat it returnsexampleswhat goes wrong
OCReach word with its box on the pageTesseract, PaddleOCR; skipped for a digital PDF0 read as O, a digit dropped from an amount
Layout modelblocks with a type, the reading order, table cellsdetectors trained on DocLayNet, Docling, cloud document servicesa table split in two, columns merged
Serialiseone text with headings, key: value lines and tables kept as tablesMarkdown or HTMLa long table cut by the context limit
Extractorone value per fieldthe question-answering model above, or a language model with a list of fieldsa distractor taken for the field
Checksaccept or reviewvalue found on the page, date and amount parse, score above the thresholda wrong value that is on the page
Each stage has its own test set. Word error rate for OCR, block and cell accuracy for layout, field accuracy for the extractor. A single end score cannot say which stage to fix.

Start with the pipeline

It needs no labels, every stage can be inspected, and either model can be replaced without touching the other.

Fine-tune for volume

One document type in the hundreds of thousands, with reviewed pages on file, is the case for a layout-aware extractor.

Keep the check on the page

Any design that generates text can write a value that is absent from the page. The check that finds the value on the page stays.

Extraction · Language model as extractor · Example

Example The extractor can be a language model with a list of fields. On 120 of the agreements it gets 97% of fields right, against 86% for the question-answering model.

share of agreements with the field right · rules and QA on 400 agreements, language model on 120 of them
 rules    question-answering model    language model, measured in the next session
What it adds. The final repayment date goes from 53% to 99%: a worked example in the prompt shows the model which date is wanted. All six fields come back as one JSON object. The interest rate does not improve: 83% against 85%.
What it gives up. The question-answering model copies a span, so its value is always on the page. A language model writes its value, so the check that the value is on the page becomes necessary.
No score comes with the answer. The accept-or-review threshold needs one. The probabilities the model gave its own tokens are the usual stand-in.
Next session builds the prompt step by step, from a plain request to this result.
Documents · Verdict

Verdict Rules were right on 56.6% of fields and never wrong when they answered. The question-answering model was right on 85.5% and wrong with confidence on some of the rest.

Rules first

Where a rule matches, take its value. It is exact, fast and explainable. Count how often no rule matches; that number is the case for a model.

A model for the rest

Send what the rules miss to a model, and keep its score. Fine-tune it on reviewed documents when the score histogram shows right and wrong answers mixed.

A person for the uncertain

Route by score and by validation checks. Store every correction with the page; those rows are the labelled data for the next model.

Layout first. Pages with columns, forms and tables go through a layout model before any extractor reads them. Stamps and signatures need an image model of their own.
Next session. The language model that extracted these six fields is built up prompt by prompt, and its answers are checked for values it made up.

A model as it comes is a starting point. On sentiment and on entities, the download lost to a model that had seen the bank’s own kind of text. A few hundred to a few thousand labels changed the result.
Measure each stage, then route. Rules where the text has a shape, a model where it does not, a score on every output, and a person for the outputs with low scores.
